title: Underwood says the FLIR could not have lost lock; active-duty WSO disagrees
summary: Merrick von Renenamp tells of Underwood says the FLIR could not have lost lock; active-duty WSO disagrees, about 2004 at Off Southern California, and relays what a named person told them. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: who's the Wizo who filmed it, he said, "Nope, there's no way the system would have lost it. I've talked to an active duty Wizo serving now and he said it's a finick."

plain: In 2004, off the coast of Southern California, Navy fliers say they ran into an unknown object, and one of them, a back-seat crew member named Chad Underwood, filmed it with the jet's FLIR, a heat-sensing camera that locks onto a target and follows it. On a podcast debate hosted by Jesse Michels, a guest named Merrick von Renenamp says Underwood told him there was no way the camera could have lost its lock on the object. Von Renenamp adds that an unnamed weapons systems officer (the crew member who runs a jet's sensors) now on active duty told him the opposite, that the system is finicky. The question matters because if the lock held, the object's sudden moves on the video would be real and not a camera glitch.
